ledger.failureMode: A project that references Microsoft.Playwright.Xunit is classified as 'xunit' by detectE2eFramework, but the Proposal-stage instruction says framework 'xunit' means there is no PageTest Page, and the xunit branch of spec-writer that the landing step calls emits a plain class with a constructor-injected fixture, takes no base class and throws unless collection and fixtureType are supplied; tests written against Microsoft.Playwright.Xunit derive from PageTest and use Page, so for those projects the authoring guidance is wrong and a new spec file either cannot be landed or is landed without the PageTest base, leaving Page undefined in the body the agent wrote.
ledger.evidence: Read, not run. (1) packages/e2e-testing/lib/e2e-framework.js:24-25 maps any package name starting with 'xunit' and the exact name 'microsoft.playwright.xunit' to xunit, and packages/e2e-testing/tests/e2e-framework.test.js:30 pins 'Microsoft.Playwright.Xunit' as xunit. (2) The text this change adds says, in packages/e2e-testing/agents/playwright-tester.yaml:61 (same sentence in agents/playwright-tester.md, packages/codex/.codex/agents/playwright-tester.toml and packages/pi/agents/playwright-tester.md): framework 'xunit' means no PageTest `Page`: build the context and page as the project's sibling tests do. The command text (commands/author-playwright-tests.yaml, Phase 3 step 2) repeats that an xunit test builds its own page. (3) packages/e2e-testing/lib/spec-writer.js scaffoldNewSpecFile (184-193) sends xunit to scaffoldXunitFile (217-251), which destructures only className, ns, collection, fixtureType and usings, throws when collection or fixtureType is missing, and emits 'public class <name>' with a '_fixture' field and no base class; baseClass is validated only for nunit. The command's landing step (commands/author-playwright-tests.yaml:226) likewise says a new xunit file needs {collection, fixtureType} copied from a sibling spec class. (4) Playwright's own documentation (https://playwright.dev/dotnet/docs/test-runners) says Playwright provides base classes for xUnit through the Microsoft.Playwright.Xunit package and shows 'using Microsoft.Playwright.Xunit; public class UnitTest1 : PageTest { [Fact] public async Task ... { await Page.GotoAsync(...); } }'. So a project on that package is routed into the core-Microsoft.Playwright-plus-[Collection]-fixture shape, the only xUnit shape the two CHANGELOG entries say is supported, and neither the command nor the agent text tells the agent to stop or ask when the sibling tests derive from PageTest. Appending to an existing xunit file still works; the break is for a new spec file. Possible fixes: stop classifying Microsoft.Playwright.Xunit as the fixture shape (return null or a separate value), or let spec-writer emit a PageTest-derived class, and make the agent text say which shape applies.

ledger.failureMode: detectE2eFramework decides NUnit versus xUnit by package-name prefix (name.startsWith('nunit') and name.startsWith('xunit') on lines 24-25), so look-alike packages that are loggers or helpers rather than test frameworks flip the flags. A csproj that lists xunit, Microsoft.Playwright and NunitXml.TestLogger sets both flags, the function returns null (neither or both), and the command turns null into the explicit framework 'nunit'. A genuine xUnit project then gets a NUnit-shaped new file, and appending to an existing xUnit file is refused with a framework-mismatch error because the explicit 'nunit' overrides the file-based inference in appendTestMethod. The same null follows when the Include attribute is written with single quotes, because only double-quoted attributes match. None of the detection tests uses a look-alike package name or a single-quoted attribute, so the false-positive side of the prefix rule is untested.

ledger.failureMode: detectE2eFramework returns 'xunit' for any project that references Microsoft.Playwright.Xunit (line 25 of e2e-framework.js, and a test pins it), but that package's documented usage is a test class deriving from its PageTest base class and using the inherited Page property.
